title: Introduce Autonomize batch crawler with cost-aware quant rollback and telemetry
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: tenant workloads vary widely and static defaults for batching, prefill/caching, and quantization cause either excessive cost or regressions in output quality. This PR ships a runtime 'batch crawler' that continuously samples tenant request shapes and synthesizes conservative batch/cache/quant profiles; it also introduces a short-circuit "quant rollback" mechanism to automatically relax aggressive quantization when quality or eval signals deteriorate. High-level summary: 1) crawler service that samples traffic, builds workload histograms and candidate batch shapes; 2) policy engine that proposes tenant-level defaults (microbatch size, prefill window, cache TTL, quant profile) and exposes them as opt-in staged rollouts; 3) quant rollback controller that watches quality signals (loss spikes, eval regression, exemplar divergence) and swaps back to safer quant tiers for affected routes; 4) telemetry changes to emit prefill hit/miss histograms, per-prefill unit-econ metrics, quant stability score, and audit events for automatic rollbacks; 5) safe guards: cooldowns, rate-limited changes, tenant isolation and canary rollout mode. Checklist: [x] unit tests for crawler sampling logic; [x] integration test harness simulating tenant workload shapes; [x] metrics and dashboards wired to observability; [x] docs and runbook for operators; [x] feature flag and canary rollout. Rollout plan: enable crawler in dry-run per-tenant for 1 week, then pilot on 5 low-latency tenants; observe unit-econ delta and quality regressions for two weeks before broad opt-in. Backwards compatibility: defaults are only suggested until tenant accepts or rollout is global; rollback is automatic and conservative. Related: ENG-2245 for crawler design, ENG-2298 for quant rollback heuristics. Impact: expected 6-12% token cost reduction for sampled pilot tenants without measurable end-user quality degradation in pilot. Monitoring: new alerts on quant stability falling below thresholds and rollback rate spikes.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Requested more explicit metric names and a histogram bucket review for prefill latency; suggested making the crawler sampling window configurable per-tenant. Author response: adjusted metric names to prefex 'econ_' and added tenant_window configuration with sane defaults, pushed new commit b6f4e90. Leah Soto: Asked to add guardrail that prevents quant rollback from happening more than once per 10 minutes per route; asked for a small e2e demonstrating rollback under a synthetic quality drop. Author response: added cooldown logic to quant_rollback controller and an e2e test that flips an eval signal; pushed commit ef4b221. Diego Morales: Concerned about persistence schema for workload histograms at scale; requested retention strategy and compaction. Author response: added compaction policy and TTL configuration, documented expected storage growth; Diego approved after verifying compaction unit tests. Final status: two approvals and CI green, ready to merge.

release_notes: Introduce an opt-in runtimes feature: 'Autonomize batch crawler' to recommend tenant-level batching/caching/quant defaults and an automatic quant rollback controller that reverts aggressive quant profiles on detected quality regressions. Includes telemetry and dashboards. Rollout gated behind feature-flag and tenant opt-in.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover histogram aggregation, candidate profile selection, and rollback cooldown logic. Integration harness simulates variable sequence-length traffic and verifies recommended batch shapes reduce avg token cost in dry-run mode by ~9% in synthetic workloads. Added e2e that triggers rollback via synthetic eval regression and verifies safe fallback within configured cooldown. Load tests show crawler overhead <1% p95 latency impact when sampling at configured default rate.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: econ.autonomize.enabled default false. Helm value: econ.autonomize.sample_rate (default 0.02) and cooldown_ms for rollback (default 600000). Recommended pilot steps and dashboard links documented in runbook. If rollback rate exceeds 5% of routes in pilot, disable auto-apply and investigate via quant_stability metric.
changelog_entry: Added autonimized batching/caching defaults and quant rollback automation with telemetry. (ENG-2245, ENG-2298).
